family: Structured and candidate-span extraction, including dates and document structure
source: Candidate and structured extraction row of the build-spec pattern table
description: Measures whether the non-generative decision API can select a verbatim candidate span, decompose a date expression into parts that code resolves, and recover document structure from extracted lines. Three families share the file: span selection with an explicit none option, date-component Choices, and autoformat join Nouls plus block-type Choices with speculative companions. Day of month is deliberately split into a ten-day band Choice (day_tens) and a final-digit Choice (day_unit) because 31 day options would exceed the 26 single-token label ceiling; a miss on one of those two questions is a split-encoding failure and must not be read as a general date failure. Report per-question exact match plus a whole-record exact match rate over all questions of a case, precision and recall of the none option on the span cases, and the date cases split by gold mode so that relative-mode and absolute-mode accuracy stay separate numbers. Date targets stop at the component Choices and never at a resolved calendar date, because the cookbook keeps calendar arithmetic in code; relative-mode and absolute-mode accuracy should be reported separately. The suite does not measure string generation, retrieval, arithmetic, calibration of the returned probabilities, or any behaviour outside a single 2048-token prefill per question.

cases.name: invoice-total-vs-subtotal
cases.rationale: The document labels one line 'Total due on this invoice' and states that the prior balance is invoiced separately, so the grand-total span is the gold and the prior balance is excluded by explicit text, not arithmetic.

The second sentence confirms the current week is excluded. [contested in audit: the gold week_after_next only follows if 'this Friday' already sits in the week after the current one, which the state never fixes. Read plainly, 'this Friday' is the current week's Friday and 'the Friday after that one' is next_week. The option descriptions count weeks from the current week and the state supplies no reference date, so both labels are defensible and the case is graded separately.]
